newsitem.title: INDIA: India cabinet extends direct rule in Uttar Pradesh.
newsitem.headline: India cabinet extends direct rule in Uttar Pradesh.

text.p: The Indian cabinet decided on Thursday to extend New Delh's direct rule in the populous state of Uttar Pradesh where local polls last week returned a hung assembly, the Press Trust of India news agency said.
The decision has to be ratified by President Shankar Dayal Sharma before midnight when direct rule imposed last year expires.
The agency did not say for how long a period direct rule over Uttar Pradesh was extended.
The Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) emerged from the elections as the largest single party with 177 seats but failed to clinch a majority in the 425-seat state assembly.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's United Front coalition, led by federal Defence Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav, ended second in the race with 134 members.
The Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) of former chief minister Mayawati (Eds: one name), representing the lowest Hindu castes, won 67 seats, while its Congress party ally clinched 33.
No party or alliance has been able to cobble together a coalition to stake a viable claim to form a government in Uttar Pradesh.
